name: SDWPF causal wind-regime wiki
description: Observable wind-turbine operating scenes used as frozen semantic anchors. Every scene must be inferable from the historical SCADA window only.

scenes.title: Normal stable production
scenes.prompt: The turbine is operating normally. Recent wind speed and active power are comparatively stable, with no clear ramp, abrupt gust, low-wind idle state, rated-power saturation, or high-wind low-power anomaly. Favor smooth short-horizon continuation while allowing small corrections.

scenes.title: Normal upward power ramp
scenes.prompt: Recent active power shows a sustained upward ramp under changing wind conditions. Preserve the rising direction but avoid unlimited extrapolation near rated power. Use only the observed SCADA history.

scenes.title: Normal downward power ramp
scenes.prompt: Recent active power shows a sustained downward ramp. Preserve the falling direction while respecting the zero-power floor and possible recovery. Use only the observed SCADA history.

scenes.title: Gusty or turbulent transition
scenes.prompt: Recent wind speed is highly variable or contains an abrupt jump. Treat the operating state as uncertain and rapidly changing; emphasize recent wind dynamics and avoid overconfident smooth extrapolation.
observable_evidence: large recent wind-speed standard deviation or step

scenes.title: High wind with unexpectedly low power
scenes.prompt: Observed wind is sufficient for generation but recent active power is unexpectedly low. This is an observable state, not a confirmed diagnosis; possible explanations include control action, curtailment, shutdown, or sensor/fault conditions. Favor conservative power continuation until the history shows recovery.

scenes.title: Rated-power saturation
scenes.prompt: Recent active power is near the turbine rated-power ceiling. Respect saturation and avoid forecasts above the physical upper bound while remaining responsive to an observed decline.

scenes.title: Low-wind idle state
scenes.prompt: Recent wind speed is below or near cut-in and active power is low. Favor a near-zero forecast unless the observed wind history already indicates a clear recovery.
